'''Péter R. Surján''' (born August 30, 1955<ref name="cv">{{cite web |url= http://coulson.chem.elte.hu/surjan/cv.html|title=Curriculum vitae  |author=Péter Surján |date= June 15, 2017|website=The homepage of Péter Surján  |access-date=August 16, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170818214623/http://coulson.chem.elte.hu/surjan/cv.html |url-status= live|archive-date=August 18, 2017}}</ref>) is a [[Hungary|Hungarian]] [[theoretical chemist]] who is known for his research on application of the theory of [[second quantization]] in [[quantum chemistry]]. 

In 2016 a [[festschrift]] from [[Theoretical Chemistry Accounts]] journal was published in his name<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Szabados  |first1= Ágnes |last2= Kállay|first2= Mihály |last3= Szalay| first3= Péter G. |date= 2016 |title= Preface to the special collection of theoretical chemistry accounts in honour of Péter R. Surján|journal=Theoretical Chemistry Accounts |volume= 135|pages= 19|doi=10.1007/s00214-015-1771-y |doi-access= free}}</ref> which is also published as a book in [[Highlights in Theoretical Chemistry]] series by the [[Springer Nature]].<ref>{{cite book|title=Péter R. Surján: A Festschrift from Theoretical Chemistry Accounts|year=2016|editor1-last=Szabados|editor1-first=Ágnes |editor2-last=Kállay|editor2-first=Mihály|editor3-last=Szalay|editor3-first=Péter G.|series=Highlights in Theoretical Chemistry|volume=12|publisher=Springer-Verlag Berlin Heidelberg| pages=266| doi=10.1007/978-3-662-49825-5| isbn=9783662498255|s2cid=183014238}}</ref> He is currently a professor and a former dean of the [[ELTE Faculty of Science|Faculty of Science]] of the [[Eötvös Loránd University]].<ref name="dean">{{cite web |url=http://ttk.elte.hu/vezetoseg|title=Természettudományi Kar - A Kar vezetése és elérhetősége|language=Hungarian|website=Magyar Tudományos Akadémia |access-date=August 17, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170818214236/http://ttk.elte.hu/vezetoseg |url-status=dead|archive-date=August 18, 2017}}</ref>

==Academic career==
Surján received his Master's degree in physics in 1978 and his PhD in quantum chemistry in 1981, both from ([[Eötvös Loránd University]].{{citation needed|date=December 2023}} In 1986, he was a [[Candidate of Science]].<ref name="MTA">{{cite web |url= http://mta.hu/koztestuleti_tagok?PersonId=11710|title=Az MTA köztestületének tagjai|language=Hungarian|website=Magyar Tudományos Akadémia |access-date=August 17, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170818175242/http://mta.hu/koztestuleti_tagok?PersonId=11710 |url-status= live|archive-date=August 18, 2017}}</ref> From there, he worked at the [[Technical University of Budapest]] as a senior researcher in physics from 1990 to 1995 before moving to Eötvös Loránd University, where he has been since. He has taught in the Department of Theoretical Chemistry since 1991, becoming a full professor in 1998, and has been the Director of the Bolyai College (2007-2012) and the Institute of Chemistry (2008-2012).{{citation needed|date=December 2023}} He was also the dean of the Faculty of Science.<ref name="dean" />

Surján is a member of the [[Hungarian Academy of Sciences]] (1998)<ref name="MTA" /> and has been on the editorial boards of the ''[[Journal of Mathematical Chemistry]]''<ref>{{cite web |url= https://www.springer.com/chemistry/physical+chemistry/journal/10910?detailsPage=editorialBoard|title=Editorial Board|website=Journal of Mathematical Chemistry |publisher= Springer International Publishing AG. |access-date=August 17, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170818214402/http://www.springer.com/chemistry/physical+chemistry/journal/10910?detailsPage=editorialBoard |url-status= live|archive-date=August 18, 2017}}</ref> and ''[[Interdisciplinary Sciences: Computational Life Sciences]]''.<ref>{{cite web |url= https://www.springer.com/life+sciences/systems+biology+and+bioinformatics/journal/12539?detailsPage=editorialBoard|title=Editorial Board|website=Interdisciplinary Sciences: Computational Life Sciences |publisher= Springer International Publishing AG. |access-date=August 17, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170818173214/http://www.springer.com/life+sciences/systems+biology+and+bioinformatics/journal/12539?detailsPage=editorialBoard |url-status= live|archive-date=August 18, 2017}}</ref> He has also been a guest editor for the ''[[International Journal of Quantum Chemistry]]''.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Lendvay |first1= György |last2= Surján |first2= Péter R.|last3= Szalay|first3= Péter G.  |date= 2009 |title=Preface to the Special Issue of IJQC dedicated to the 65th birthday of Professor István Mayer |journal=International Journal of Quantum Chemistry |volume= 109|pages= 2039|doi=10.1002/qua.22274}}</ref> Surján has published more than 190 papers in his scientific career. His first paper was published in 1980.

==Selected publications==
===Papers===
* "Optical Rotatory Strength Calculation by Evaluating the Gradient Matrix through the Equation of Motion", ''[[Theoretica Chimica Acta]]'' 55, 103 (1980); {{doi|10.1007/BF00576955}}
* "Higher excitations in coupled-cluster theory", ''[[The Journal of Chemical Physics]]'' 115, 2945 (2001); {{doi| 10.1063/1.1383290}}
* "A general state-selective multireference coupled-cluster algorithm", ''[[The Journal of Chemical Physics]]'' 117, 980 (2002); {{doi|10.1063/1.1483856}}
* "Computing coupled-cluster wave functions with arbitrary excitations", ''[[The Journal of Chemical Physics]]'' 113, 1359 (2000); {{doi|10.1063/1.481925}}
* "An observable-based interpretation of electronic wavefunctions: application to “hypervalent” molecules", ''[[Computational and Theoretical Chemistry]]'' 255, 9 (1992); {{doi|10.1016/0166-1280(92)85003-4}}

*{{cite book|title= Correlation and Localization|year=1999|editor1-last=Surján|editor1-first=Péter R.|series=Topics in Current Chemistry|volume=203|publisher=Springer-Verlag Berlin Heidelberg|pages=236|doi=10.1007/3-540-48972-X|isbn=978-3-540-65754-5}}
